title: When the Lantern Burns
premise: Petra Whitlock, apprentice to a mapmaker who died under suspicious circumstances while charting the river valley, must complete his forbidden atlas before the magistrate's men return in spring. When the seasonal bridge closes, a wounded stranger named Elias Row crosses the ice instead — a fugitive carrying proof that the master was murdered to bury what the maps revealed: a drowned village and the names of those the flood was arranged to erase. As Petra and Elias finish the atlas together, love and suspicion grow between them, and Petra must choose between the silences that kept her safe for twenty years and a justice the law will never grant. The atlas is completed and smuggled out before the workshop burns, the truth published abroad, and Petra, having lost nearly everything, finally speaks her master's name aloud.
about_author: Yara Lockridge is a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing river surveys and land disputes in municipal collections, where she first encountered maps that had been quietly altered. She writes historical fiction about the paper trails people leave behind and the courage it takes to read them honestly.

chapters.title: The Weight of Blank Paper
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the frozen workshop, Petra grinds ink and surveys her dead master Aldous Whitlock's unfinished atlas, hiding the dangerous final folios beneath floorboards. Establishes her habit of silence and her fear that the magistrate will return for the rest. Beat: grief braided with dread.

chapters.title: Twenty Years of Careful Quiet
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, with flashback. We learn how Aldous took her in as an orphan, taught her draftsmanship, and warned her never to ask about the valley's drowned village of Merrow's Bend. The magistrate's clerk visits, asking polite, chilling questions. Beat: the cost of obedience made visible.

chapters.title: The Bridge Closes
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The ferryman chains the bridge for winter, severing the town from the world. Petra feels both trapped and, for once, safe — no one can come for the atlas. She begins inking the coastal sheets. Beat: false security before the turn.

chapters.title: A Man Out of the River Ice
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At dawn she finds Elias Row half-frozen on the bank, having crossed on foot. He carries a satchel he refuses to open and a wound he refuses to explain. She hides him in the map chest loft before the constable's rounds. Beat: fear and fascination entwined.

chapters.title: What the Satchel Holds
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. He reveals Aldous's original survey of Merrow's Bend — proof the flood was engineered to erase debts and witnesses — and a list of names. Aldous was his uncle's friend; Elias is the last living person from the village. Beat: the silence Petra kept becomes complicity.

chapters.title: The Master's Last Journey
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, flashback. Reconstructing Aldous's final survey trip through his marginalia, Petra realizes he knew he was being followed and hid the true plates deliberately — and that her own apprenticeship was his contingency plan. Beat: devastating re-reading of the past.

chapters.title: Ink Under Fingernails
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Working side by side through the nights, Petra and Elias fall into rhythm and then into feeling. She teaches him cartography; he teaches her the names of the drowned. Beat: tenderness as resistance.

chapters.title: The Clerk Returns Early
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The magistrate's clerk arrives before the thaw, claiming the bridge ice made the road passable. He searches the workshop with courteous thoroughness and nearly finds the floorboard cache. Beat: terror in a drawing room.

chapters.title: A Map That Lies
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. To buy time, Petra offers the clerk the official atlas — the sanitized version — while Elias copies the true plates in a hidden garret. Elias struggles with rage: the lie that saved them once erased his village. Beat: moral friction between the lovers.

chapters.title: Names on the Margins
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. Petra discovers her own mother's name on Elias's list — she was of Merrow's Bend, and Aldous took Petra in because he owed the dead. Her whole identity reorders in one night. Beat: grief transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: The Ferryman's Oath
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The pair recruit the old ferryman, who watched the flood as a boy and has kept his own silence for twenty years. His confession, given over brandy, becomes their first testimony. Beat: the dam of communal silence cracking.

chapters.title: Winter Fair
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. At the town's winter fair the magistrate himself appears, charming and watchful, and dances with Petra while his men search the workshop again. She must smile through the conversation of a man she now knows ordered her master's death. Beat: dread wearing velvet.

chapters.title: Betrayal in Small Kindnesses
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. A neighbor Petra trusted — the woman who brings her bread — reports an unfamiliar man in the loft. The constable takes Elias's satchel of copies; only the master plates remain hidden. Beat: the intimacy of small towns as a weapon.

chapters.title: Interrogation by Lamplight
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. The clerk detains Petra, not with charges but with questions about her parentage, revealing he has always known who she is. He offers her the atlas's completion in exchange for the original plates — and her continued silence. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: The Choice of the Ink
chapters.summary: Dual POV. Petra refuses, and Elias, freed by the ferryman's diversion, returns through the storm. The lovers argue bitterly: he wants to flee with the plates; she insists the atlas must be finished and seen. Beat: love tested against duty's mirror image.

chapters.title: What Aldous Died For
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the master's locked drawer they find his letter: he stayed to finish the atlas knowing they would kill him, because a map that exists cannot be unmade. Petra resolves to complete it in his hand, forgery and inheritance at once. Beat: resolve forged from grief.

chapters.title: The Last Folio
chapters.summary: Dual POV. A montage of nights: inking the drowned village street by street, Elias dictating names, Petra lettering them into the margins where no official would think to look. The atlas becomes a ledger of the dead disguised as geography. Beat: sacred, exhausted creation.

chapters.title: Smoke on the North Wind
chapters.summary: Elias's POV. The magistrate learns the truth is nearly finished and moves to burn the workshop before the thaw. The ferryman warns them at midnight; they have one night to save the plates. Beat: the noose tightening.

chapters.title: Fire and Ice
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, climax part one. The workshop burns. Petra and Elias carry the atlas across the frozen river under pursuit, the ice groaning, the firelight behind them. The ferryman holds the constables at the bank with his boat chains. Beat: pure kinetic peril.

chapters.title: The Crossing
chapters.summary: Elias's POV, climax part two. The ice breaks; Petra goes into the river clutching the atlas case. Elias pulls her out; the plates survive, sealed in wax and oilcloth as Aldous taught her. The magistrate's men turn back, believing the work destroyed. Beat: near-loss and hard-won survival.

chapters.title: Spring, and the World Reading
chapters.summary: Petra's POV. In the capital, a printer sympathetic to Elias's cause publishes the atlas with its marginal names. Copies circulate; an inquiry opens; the magistrate is arrested on the ferryman's testimony and the clerk turns crown's evidence. Beat: justice arriving through paper, not law's goodwill.

chapters.title: Speaking the Names
chapters.summary: Petra's POV, resolution. Petra and Elias return to the valley in spring, rebuild the workshop as a school of honest cartography, and stand at the drowned village's shoreline. She reads the names aloud, her mother's last. Beat: grief answered, silence ended, love chosen freely.
